KEYS · Electronic test and design economics

Conditional results

Conditional bear/base/bull values are $37.33/$129.14/$251.28 per common share, at the July 31, 2026 capital anchor using August 27 shares and information through October 19. No probabilities, expected value, current quote, upside, expected return or recommendation are supplied.

Source 1 · Source 2

Three dates and eligibility

July 31, 2026 is the capital and discount origin; exact shares are August 27, a real 27-day mismatch; information cutoff is October 19. Ten rolling annual periods end July 2027–2036, not October fiscal years. This is a dated conditional operating-value study, not a current price target or historical backtest. Entering a quote cannot refresh the capital bridge or clear the current-target gate.

Source 1 · Source 2

Business and durable drivers

Keysight sells electronic design, emulation, validation, manufacturing-test instruments, software and services. CSG serves communications and aerospace/defense/government; EISG serves semiconductor, general electronics, automotive and energy. AI networks are a demand driver, not a separately audited pure-AI revenue stream. Customer R&D budgets, manufacturing capacity, technology transitions and defense programs all matter.

Source 1 · Source 2

TTM segment reconstruction

TTM revenue ending July 2026 is $6,582m: CSG $4,690m = FY2025 $3,726m + 9M2026 $3,700m − 9M2025 $2,736m; EISG $1,892m = $1,649m + $1,463m − $1,220m. Acquisition contributions and favorable mix limit extrapolation. The two segments have separately fading growth paths.

Source 1 · Source 2

Latest reported quarter

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $1,846m and GAAP EBIT $461m, a 24.97% margin; TTM GAAP EBIT was $1,333m and margin 20.25%. Management reported $2,091m orders, 52% core order growth and 31% core revenue growth. Wireline orders more than doubled and wireline revenue first exceeded wireless. These are issuer explanations, not independent customer-spend or backlog-conversion verification.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Ten annual observations

All ten FY2016–2025 reported/recast annual slots and 221 non-null field-source observations are retained. They are not a homogeneous organic series: Ixia and later acquisitions change perimeter; ASC606 starts FY2019; pension presentation recasts FY2017–18. FY2016 is not retroactively homogenized. Missing exact year-end common shares and old lease/debt fields remain null; weighted EPS shares do not fill them.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

Accounting and perimeter breaks

ASC606 adoption on November 1, 2018 used modified retrospective treatment; FY2017–18 comparatives remain on prior revenue guidance. Later comparative EBIT is $148m/−$394m versus original $239m/−$346m after moving pension non-service components out of operating income. FY2018 includes $709m goodwill impairment and substantial tax effects; it is not a steady-state margin proxy.

Source 1 · Source 2

Release versus audited vintages

FY2025 audited annual net income/EPS are $850m/$4.91 versus preliminary release $846m/$4.89. Both detailed revenue statements say $5,375m; the $5.37bn headline is rounded, not a $1m revision. The audit confirms the numerical difference, not its cause. Audited annual history and original release-vintage quarterly scorecards remain separate.

Source 1 · Source 2

Cash-flow definitions

CFO less gross PPE capex was $1,211m/$898m/$1,281m in FY2023/24/25. It is a descriptive levered cash-flow measure, not owner FCFF; CFO contains interest, tax, working capital and SBC addback. Issuer-reported FCF also counts government incentives. Depreciation and acquisition amortization are separate; acquisition cash amounts can be recast in later comparisons.

Source 1 · Source 2

All eleven guidance pairs

All eleven Q1 FY2024–Q3 FY2026 pairs preserve original preceding-release revenue and non-GAAP diluted EPS ranges, subsequent release actuals, distinct publication dates, public links and six-field provenance. Both actuals exceed their original upper bounds in every pair. This is not consensus outperformance, proof of no interim revisions or a calibrated management premium. Short-term execution and conservative range-setting cannot establish decade-long forecast precision.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

Quality of reported beats

Q3 FY2024 $1.57 EPS includes a $0.16 tax benefit; management’s $1.41 excluding it still beats $1.36. Q2 FY2026 reported $1,717m/$2.87 becomes management-adjusted $1,758m/$2.58 excluding tariff/refund effects, still above $1,710m/$2.33. Use explicit $1,758m, not $1,757m inferred from an approximate $40m. These are issuer adjustments, not an independent quality-of-earnings conclusion.

Source 1 · Source 2

Prospective FY2026 outlook

At cutoff, August 18 Q4 FY2026 guidance remains prospective: revenue $1,930–1,950m, non-GAAP EPS $3.34–3.40, approximately 172m weighted diluted shares. Management’s midpoint implies about 32% FY2026 sales and 60% EPS growth, with 80–90% of $100m synergies at fiscal-year exit run rate. Initial FY2026 ex-acquisition growth of at least 7% and later total growth above 20%, high-20s and 32% have different scopes. Do not score July 2027 rolling revenue against October 2026 fiscal guidance.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

Acquisition discipline

Spirent closed October 15, 2025 for $1,564m consideration, with $399m divestiture proceeds; Synopsys Optical Solutions Group and PowerArtist also expand scope. Nine-month FY2026 Spirent integration/acquisition cost was $75m. Already-paid consideration is reflected in opening capital and is not charged again. A future 1%-of-sales acquisition/intangible-renewal allowance is an estimate, not historical purchase price or funding for an unannounced major deal.

Source 1 · Source 2

Economic profitability

Economic margins retain R&D, SBC as cash-equivalent replacement compensation and acquired amortization without a separate addback. Bear margins start 16%, trough 15%, and reach 20%; base starts 25% and reaches 27%; bull starts 27% and reaches 30%. Base exceeds TTM GAAP 20.25% and needs durable gains from the latest quarter’s 24.97%; bull is especially demanding. Management adjusted segment margins are not interchangeable with this economic EBIT.

Source 1 · Source 2

Two segment growth paths

CSG and EISG are separately projected. Bear begins −12%/−10%, then −4%/−2%, recovering toward 2%; base begins 18%/8%, then 12%/7%, fading to 3%; bull begins 25%/12%, then 18%/10%, fading to 3.5%. These are analyst scenarios. Acquisition annualization, product mix and customer spending cycles prevent indefinite extension of current growth; no scenario probabilities are estimated.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Investment and working capital

Each year gross physical capex is 3.5% of sales, depreciation 2%, acquisition/intangible renewal 1%, marginal NWC 18% of revenue change and operating cash 8% of sales. R&D remains expensed. Reinvestment is the greater of these operating needs and the phased sustainable-ROIC requirement; net investment is not gross capex. These are modeling conventions, not independently established maintenance-capital needs.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Capital and claims bridge

July cash $2,605m − face debt $2,550m − retirement/post-retirement reserve $76m − swap reserve $20m − minimum operating cash $526.56m gives a −$567.56m bridge. Debt carrying value is $2,517m. Restricted cash $17m and long-term investments $188m receive zero bridge value. Operating leases $53m current/$176m noncurrent are not financing debt while rent remains in operating margins; deducting both would double count.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

Exact shares and award limits

Exact August 27 common shares are 170,244,745, or 170.244745m, 27 days after the balance anchor. No ADR or alternate-class conversion applies. Nine-month diluted EPS average 173m and Q4 guidance diluted 172m are not point-in-time common shares. Existing awards are not valued grant by grant; retained SBC and the separate 3% share stress are a convention and diagnostic, not exact settlement or a maximum dilution bound.

Source 1 · Source 2

Debt and coupon mechanics

Scheduled principal is $700m April 2027, $500m October 2029, $750m July 2030 and $600m October 2034. Principal reduces treasury when paid and equity once at inception, not FCFF. Full coupons in maturity years are conservative timing simplifications. The $600m fixed-to-floating swap makes 4.95% approximate. A +200bp coupon shock leaves operating EV unchanged but reduces base minimum headroom to $2,211.1401m; WACC risk is separate.

Source 1 · Source 2

Funding detector and suppression

Annual cash starts after pension/swap reserves, retains cash, pays debt service and tests an 8%-of-sales floor. Shortfalls borrow up to a hypothetical $750m then issue equity at hypothetical $100/share with 5% fees. Neither is guaranteed funding. Emergency-debt repayment/refinancing and the revolver’s April 21, 2031 expiry are unmodeled; intra-year troughs and detailed covenants are absent. Any external funding suppresses headline common value. Funded dilution diagnostics are never fair value; the module is a funding-need detector.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Tax provision versus cash tax

Nine-month July 2026 income-tax provision is $66m; net cash income taxes paid are $127m from supplemental cash-flow disclosure. They are different measures and neither is the modeled tax rate. The model charges 22% on positive economic EBIT, with no immediate tax benefit for losses and no perpetuation of refunds, investment gains or temporary tariffs.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

Discount rates and returns

Bear/base/bull WACC is 12%/10%/8.5%, terminal growth 2%/3%/3.5% and terminal incremental ROIC 12%/18%/22%. These are analyst judgments, not fitted live market rates or probabilities. WACC and ROIC must both exceed growth; finite, domain and convergence tests apply. Current stock prices never calibrate the cases.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Two terminal investment floors

Terminal reinvestment is max(NOPAT × growth / ROIC, physical net investment + acquisition renewal + incremental NWC + incremental operating cash). Both floors must hold; growth in both segments converges. Positive terminal earnings and distributable FCFF are required. Bear’s operating floor can exceed its ROIC floor, so never force investment down to a pure ROIC formula. Terminal cash flows are 41.88%/55.04%/66.78% of bear/base/bull EV.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Scenario uncertainty

The three cases are assumptions, not a probability distribution or confidence interval; base is not expected value. Margin judgments dominate. The source contains 20 WACC/g cells, four margin shocks, a 3% share diagnostic, a floating-coupon shock and two complete funding stresses. Invalid and funded headline outputs remain unavailable. Simulations require manual initiation and cannot turn conditional parameters into estimated returns.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3 · Source 4

Unresolved claim and semantic limits

Existing award claims lack grant-level valuation; annual liquidity lacks intra-year detail; operating and acquisition investment requirements are estimates. Restricted cash and long-term investments stay fixed at zero inclusion. The source accepts some metadata that is not economically implemented; arbitrary new semantic inputs are not admitted. A current target needs separately reviewed current capital, exact shares, claims/awards, material events and financing/stub assumptions.

Independent admission audit v2

Independent audit v2 admits the original v1 study PASS WITH LIMITATIONS. It verified hashes/bytes for 113 files; independently recomputed all 30 forecast rows, scalars and sensitivities; checked 23 invalid inputs; reconciled 221 non-null facts; and parsed original release HTML to verify all 11 pairs. It re-opened key official filings and the Q3 release. This evidence audit is not financial-statement assurance, current-target approval, physical-capital validation or adapter/deployment certification.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

Evidence limits

The bounded official-site search found no later earnings outlook, but does not prove no interim update or material event. There was no exhaustive interim-release, call-Q&A, independent interview, customer or competitor cross-check. Prepared remarks are management-controlled statements. Historical source tracing does not re-audit every annual disclosure. Public Robinhood support is not account/jurisdiction eligibility. Corporate originals remain linked; only curated derived research is packaged.

Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3

What requires fresh review

Monitor organic CSG order conversion after acquisitions annualize, AI network/test demand durability, export controls and tariffs, R&D intensity, integration costs, working capital/deferred revenue, acquisitions/buybacks and shares versus SBC. Current target, upside, expected return, recommendation and ranking stay unavailable even if a quote is entered. Only an independently reviewed refreshed bridge, award treatment, events and financing assumptions can reopen consideration.

两道终值投资底线

终值再投资取「NOPAT×增长／ROIC」与「实物净投资＋收购更新＋增量营运资本＋增量经营现金」较大者，两道底线均需满足，两分部增长需收敛。终值利润及可分配 FCFF 须为正。熊情景经营底线可高于 ROIC 底线，不能强行把投资压至单纯 ROIC 公式。终值现金流占熊／基准／牛 EV 的 41.88%／55.04%／66.78%。

来源 1 · 来源 2 · 来源 3 · 来源 4

情景不确定性

三个情景是条件假设，不是概率分布或置信区间；基准不等于期望值。利润率判断影响最大。来源含 20 个 WACC／增长格点、四个利润率冲击、3% 股数诊断、浮动票息冲击及两组完整融资压力。无效及需融资主要输出保持不可用。模拟需手动启动，不能把条件参数变成预计收益。

未解决请求权及语义限制

现有奖励缺少逐笔估值，年度流动性缺少年内细节，经营及收购投资需求为估计。受限现金和长期投资纳入值固定为零。来源会接受某些未在经济计算中实现的元数据，不因此允许任意新增语义输入。当前目标价需要另行复核当期资本、精确股数、请求权／奖励、重大事件及融资／期间现金流假设。

独立准入复核 v2

独立复核 v2 对原 v1 研究结论为「有保留限制通过」：核对 113 文件哈希／字节，独立重算全部 30 预测行、标量及敏感性，检查 23 个无效输入，对账 221 个非空事实，并解析原新闻稿 HTML 核验十一组记录；还重开关键官方申报及第三季稿。此证据复核不是财务报表审计保证、当前目标价许可、实物资本验证或适配器／部署认证。

证据限制

有限官方站点搜索未找到更晚业绩展望，但不能证明没有期中更新或重大事件。未穷尽期中稿、电话会问答、独立访谈、客户或竞争者交叉核实；预备发言为管理层控制内容。历史来源追溯不等于重审每项年报披露。Robinhood 公开支持不等于特定账户／地区资格。公司原件仅提供链接，打包只含精选派生研究。

来源 1 · 来源 2 · 来源 3

需要重新复核的事项

观察收购并表满周年后的 CSG 有机订单转化、AI 网络／测试需求持续性、出口管制与关税、研发强度、整合成本、营运资本／递延收入、收购／回购及股数相对薪酬。即使输入股价，当前目标、上涨空间、预期收益、投资建议及排名均不可用。只有经独立复核的最新桥接、奖励处理、事件及融资假设才能重新考虑。
